_comment: Edit(./**) covers every file-editing tool, Write and MultiEdit included.
Naming those separately does nothing: only Edit(path) rules are consulted
by file permission checks, so Write(./**) and MultiEdit(./**) were inert
and Claude Code warned about them on every start.
Bash is allow-listed to read-only inspection rather than granted wholesale.
A Bash deny-list cannot protect a file: 'cat secret' is one spelling among
head, tail, less, xxd, awk, python -c and a shell redirect, so denying cat
buys the appearance of protection and not the fact of it. Anything absent
from this list prompts instead, which is the actual control.
